channel.title: Sidharth Sajith — Blog
channel.description: Robotics & Automation Engineer — AI, Computer Vision, Embedded Systems

item.title: A Robot That Remembers Where You Left Your Wrench
item.description: No cloud, no LiDAR, no RFID — just a Jetson, some VLMs, and a stubborn belief that robots should find your stuff offline.

item.title: How I Accidentally Automated My Blog Posts
item.description: Discovering OpenCode, agentic multimodal AI, and a free open-weights model that turns my messy brain-dumps into posts worth publishing.

item.title: How a $400 Phone Learned to Drive
item.description: A Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 has three brains. Splitting driving workloads across its GPU, NPU, and CPU is how a phone becomes a self-driving stack.

item.title: Meet Albirr, the Robot That Remembers Your Face
item.description: A Raspberry Pi 5 robot that tracks who walks in, greets them in Malayalam, and talks back — without ever freezing up.

item.title: We Built a Robot That Yells at You for Slouching
item.description: An ESP32, a custom posture net, and an emotion CNN walk into a room. Then it starts buzzing and texting you about your life choices.

item.title: We Nearly Nuked a GPU to Teach a Rover to Read Traffic Lights
item.description: Overclocked into oblivion, drowning in VRAM, and a 20GB RAM tantrum — the unglamorous story of getting YOLO26 to actually run on a rover.

item.title: The Plant Doctor With a Bouncer at the Door
item.description: Why a disease-detection model calls your steering wheel 'mildew' — and how a cloud guardrail, a fallback, and an ESP32 pump fix it.
